title: SIEM Integration Foundation — Splunk, Elastic, and Azure Sentinel
goal: Push AegisPT findings and run events to enterprise SIEM platforms so security operations teams see pentest findings alongside live threat data in the tools they already live in.
scope: Extend the existing integration framework (from backlog-38) with three SIEM providers: (1) Splunk HEC (HTTP Event Collector): push findings as Splunk events via POST to the HEC endpoint with a structured JSON payload. Maps finding severity to Splunk alert level. (2) Elastic (Elasticsearch/Kibana): push findings as documents to a configurable index via the Elasticsearch REST API. Maps finding fields to ECS (Elastic Common Schema) fields so findings appear correctly in pre-built Kibana dashboards. (3) Azure Sentinel: push findings as custom log entries via the Azure Monitor Log Ingestion API. Maps findings to the Azure Sentinel Incident schema where applicable. Each integration is: stored in the existing integration_configurations table with encrypted credentials, triggered on run completion and on new critical finding, configurable per engagement, and clearly labeled as 'pentest findings from AegisPT' in the destination system. Also add optional Sigma rule export per finding (from the existing detection_engineering block) directly to the configured SIEM.
generation_reason: XM Cyber, Pentera, and NodeZero all integrate with enterprise SIEMs. Security operations teams want pentest findings in their SIEM alongside threat intel and alerts — not in a separate platform. SIEM integration is a standard requirement in enterprise procurement. Splunk + Elastic + Azure Sentinel covers 80%+ of enterprise SIEM deployments.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Push-only integrations. AegisPT never reads from SIEMs. Credentials encrypted. Push happens on run completion or critical finding — no continuous polling. Each push is labeled as coming from AegisPT to avoid confusion with live threat data.

success_criteria: Splunk HEC integration pushes findings as structured events on run completion.
Elastic integration pushes findings mapped to ECS schema.
Azure Sentinel integration pushes findings to custom log table.
All three integrations use encrypted credential storage.
Critical finding triggers immediate push to configured SIEMs.
Push events are labeled as 'aegispt-pentest-finding' source in destination system.
Sigma rules from detection_engineering block can be exported to configured SIEM.
Tests cover push, credential encryption, failure handling, and finding mapping.
must_not_touch: Storing SIEM credentials in plain text
pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: All three SIEM push integrations work with mock endpoints.
